title: Ramayana: Part 1 tax-free in West Bengal: CM confirms exemption for Ranbir Kapoor starrer
raw_summary:
Ramayana: Part 1, directed by Nitesh Tiwari and headlined by Ranbir Kapoor, has received a significant boost ahead of its theatrical release, with West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari confirming that the mythological film will be made tax-free in the state. Speaking to ANI, the Chief Minister also referred to films such as The Kerala Story, The Kashmir Files and The Bengal Files while discussing the decision, and indicated that more mythological stories could make their way to the big screen in the coming years.

“The Ramayana film has been made tax-free. The Kerala Story, The Kashmir Files and The Bengal Files, all of these will be or have been made tax-free, and the same will apply to 'Ramayana'. In the days to come, we will see films on Shri Krishna and Arjuna, as well as the Mahabharata,” the West Bengal CM told ANI.

The announcement could make Ramayana: Part 1 more accessible to audiences across West Bengal, potentially supporting its theatrical prospects in a key market. The exemption is expected to draw attention to the film’s release in Kolkata and other parts of the state, although the precise implementation and impact on ticket prices will depend on the applicable tax arrangements.

Conceived as the first instalment of a planned two-part cinematic saga, Ramayana: Part 1 is a Hindi-language mythological film based on the ancient Sanskrit epic attributed to Valmiki. Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, who has co-written the screenplay with Shridhar Raghavan, the film will bring the story of Prince Rama of Ayodhya, his exile and the trials surrounding his journey to the big screen on an ambitious scale.

The film features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, with Sai Pallavi portraying Sita. Kannada superstar Yash, widely known for his work in the K.G.F franchise, takes on the role of Ravana. Ravi Dubey will portray Lakshmana, adding another prominent name to the film’s ensemble.

The supporting cast includes Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman and Anupam Kher as Maharishi Vashistha. The film also features Kajal Aggarwal as Mandodari, Rakul Preet Singh as Surpanakha, Vivek Oberoi as Meghnada, also known as Indrajit, and Kunal Kapoor as Lord Indra.

Further additions to the ensemble include Adinath Kothare as Bharata, Lara Dutta as Kaikeyi and Indira Krishnan as Kausalya. Veteran actor Arun Govil, who became synonymous with Lord Rama after portraying the character in Ramanand Sagar’s iconic 1987 television series, will play King Dasharatha in the upcoming film. His casting adds a nostalgic dimension to a project revisiting one of Indian mythology’s most enduring stories.

Ramayana: Part 1 is being mounted on an ambitious scale by producer Namit Malhotra, associated with visual effects company DNEG, and Yash. The production aims to bring the epic’s characters, settings and pivotal events to life through large-scale visual effects and an expansive cinematic treatment.

The film’s music is being composed by A. R. Rahman and renowned German composer Hans Zimmer, bringing together two internationally recognised composers for the project.

With the West Bengal Chief Minister confirming the tax-free status of Ramayana, the film has gained an additional talking point ahead of its theatrical arrival.

title: Police Company release date: Ram Gopal Varma’s crime saga starring Harshvardhan Rane to hit theatres on June 4, 2027
raw_summary:
Filmmaker Ram Gopal Varma is returning to the Mumbai underworld with Police Company, an upcoming crime saga that will explore the city’s turbulent gang wars from the perspective of law enforcement. T-Series, in association with RGV Company Production, has officially announced the theatrical release date of the action thriller. Starring Harshvardhan Rane in the lead role, the film is scheduled to arrive in cinemas nationwide on June 4, 2027.

Known for exploring the underbelly of Mumbai through films like Satya and Company, Ram Gopal Varma is revisiting familiar territory with a narrative that shifts the focus from gangsters to the police officers who confronted them. In Police Company, Harshvardhan Rane will portray Daya Nayak, the Mumbai police encounter specialist whose operations became a significant part of the city’s underworld history.

Inspired by true events and real-life police officers who operated during the late 1990s and early 2000s, the film will delve into the functioning of Mumbai’s encounter squad during a particularly volatile period. The narrative is expected to explore the circumstances, aggressive policing tactics and high-stakes operations that shaped the battle against organised crime in the financial capital.

The film will revisit an era when gang-related violence and the underworld’s influence formed a significant part of Mumbai’s crime landscape. According to the film’s announcement, the story will trace the operations through which the encounter squad neutralised around 300 gangsters, eventually dismantling the underworld’s terror network in the city. By placing law enforcement at the centre of the narrative, Police Company aims to offer a different perspective on a chapter that has frequently inspired crime dramas in Hindi cinema.

Alongside Harshvardhan Rane, Police Company features Fardeen Khan, Fatima Sana Shaikh, Paresh Rawal, Saurabh Shukla, Makarand Deshpande and Ashwini Kalsekar in pivotal roles. The ensemble brings together several established performers, including actors who have previously been associated with Ram Gopal Varma’s distinctive brand of crime cinema.

Presented by Gulshan Kumar and T-Series, Police Company is directed by Ram Gopal Varma and produced by Bhushan Kumar, Krishan Kumar and Ram Gopal Varma. The film is being made under the banners of T-Series Films and RGV Company Production.

title: Mika Singh DEFENDS Daler Mehndi amid Uttarakhand event controversy, reveals he had a big operation recently: “Have you ever seen a glass of alcohol in his hand”
raw_summary:
Singer Mika Singh has come out in support of his brother and fellow singer Daler Mehndi following the controversy surrounding his performance at the Kunjapuri Mela in Uttarakhand. Calling the on-stage confrontation “disappointing”, Mika urged the media to verify allegations before publishing them as facts.

On October 20, Mika shared a video on social media along with a note wishing his followers on Dussehra. He also requested media organisations to check the facts and give artists an opportunity to present their side before reporting allegations.

Mika wrote, “The way Daler Mehndi was treated on stage was disappointing. A respected minister came on stage and made allegations about him drinking alcohol. But before publishing such claims, shouldn’t we verify the facts and give the artist a chance to present his side?” He also questioned whether a similar approach would be taken with an international act, writing, “Would anyone dare to behave like that with an international band like Coldplay?” Mika says Daler Mehndi does not drink alcohol In the video, Mika defended Daler against the allegation that he had been drinking during the performance. He said, “He has been a superstar for the last 30 years. Have you ever seen a glass of alcohol in his hand in your life?”

Mika added that Daler has been unwell and is recovering from a recent operation. “If he is not able to stand or he is not able to sing well, he was not feeling well. Because he had a big operation recently,” he said.

Mika further explained that artists sometimes honour professional commitments despite being unwell. “As much as I get sick, if I come to know that I have a show the day after tomorrow, and I have said yes, even if the budget was less or more, doesn't matter. I have to be there,” he said.

 

View this post on Instagram

  A post shared by Mika Singh (@mikasingh)

What happened at Daler Mehndi’s Uttarakhand performance? Daler Mehndi was performing at the annual Siddhpeeth Maa Kunjapuri Tourism and Development Fair in Tehri district on October 18 when Uttarakhand Cabinet Minister and local MLA Subodh Uniyal interrupted the performance.

In a video circulating online, Uniyal questioned Mehndi’s ability to sing and alleged that he appeared to be under the influence of alcohol. The minister also questioned the performance in relation to the reported fee.

Mika acknowledged that the minister could question the quality of the performance but objected to the alcohol allegation without proof.

He said, “I agree sir, you are right, but don't say that you are drinking and singing.”

Mika concluded by urging the media to be more careful with such claims, saying, “A headline can damage someone’s reputation, so please check the facts before publishing anything.”

title: SCOOP: Ramayana advance booking may get DELAYED due to revenue-sharing tussle; distributors demand 60% share in Week 1
raw_summary:
The advance booking of Ramayana, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi, was scheduled to open today, October 20, on the auspicious occasion of Dussehra. However, as of 9:30 am, barely any cinemas across the country had opened bookings for the much-awaited film. Bollywood Hungama has learned that a disagreement between distributors and exhibitors over revenue-sharing terms is said to be one of the reasons behind the delay.

A trade source told Bollywood Hungama, “Usually, for big films, the distributor's share is 52.5% in Week 1, 45% in Week 2 and 37.5% in Week 3. But the distributors of Ramayana are reportedly demanding a 60% revenue share in the first week, 50% in the second week and 40% in the third week. This is significantly higher than the usual sharing terms followed for big-budget films. As a result, exhibitors, who are understandably concerned, are reluctant to agree to these terms and negotiations are currently underway.”

The source continued, “Unless both parties arrive at a mutually acceptable agreement, the advance booking could get delayed. Everyone is keen to release Ramayana on a grand scale, but there has to be mutual consensus when it comes to commercial terms.”

It remains to be seen whether the two sides can resolve their differences soon and ensure that advance bookings begin across the country. As of 9:30 am, INOX Korum Mall in Thane is the only cinema in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region to have opened bookings for Ramayana. Another prominent multiplex where advance bookings have commenced is AMB Cinemas Kapali in Bengaluru.

Ramayana is scheduled to release worldwide on November 5.

title: Bombay High Court directs makers of Tu Hai Meri Kiran to deposit Rs. 8.85 crores before release
raw_summary:
The Bombay High Court on Monday, October 19, ruled that Echelon Productions cannot commercially release or exploit Tu Hai Meri Kiran, starring Sonakshi Sinha and Zaheer Iqbal, unless it deposits Rs. 8.85 crores along with 15% annual interest to secure the investment made by co-producer AND Movie Products LLP, as per a report by Live Law Biz. The film is scheduled to release in theatres on October 23, 2026.

Justice Amit Borkar substantially allowed AND Movie Products LLP's petition seeking protection of its investment and contractual rights in the film. The Court observed that stopping the film's release entirely would disregard the money and effort invested in its production. However, it also said that the film should not be commercially exploited without securing the co-producer's investment.

The dispute stems from a co-production agreement signed on March 27, 2024, under which both parties agreed to contribute Rs. 7.50 crore each, plus GST, towards a film budget of Rs. 15 crores plus GST. AND Movie Products stated that it invested Rs. 8.85 crore between March 2024 and January 2025 but did not receive repayment as agreed.

Under the agreement, Echelon was required to repay the investment within 13 months of signing the contract or three weeks before the film's first release, whichever came earlier. The Court held that the repayment deadline expired on April 27, 2025, and the later announcement of the film's release date could not extend it.

The dispute escalated after a cheque for Rs. 7.50 crores issued by Echelon through Vishal Rana was dishonoured in January 2026. AND Movie Products subsequently approached the High Court after the film's October release was announced.

Echelon argued that repayment depended on the film's earnings and pointed to AND Movie Products' participation in Instagram promotions. However, the Court held that promotional activities did not waive the repayment obligation or remove the requirement for the co-producer's consent before third-party exploitation agreements could be signed.

The Court directed Echelon to deposit Rs. 8.85 crores, with 15% annual interest calculated from the respective investment dates, within three working days. If it fails to comply, the film cannot be commercially exploited.

Echelon must also disclose its existing and proposed exploitation agreements, maintain film revenues in a separate designated account and provide regular accounts. The company has been directed to obtain AND Movie Products' contractual consent before entering into exploitation agreements and correct or withdraw publicity credits that do not comply with the agreed producer credits.

The Court stated that the deposited amount would be held as security and could not be withdrawn without approval from the court or an arbitral tribunal. It declined to direct Vishal Rana to personally deposit the money at this stage, noting that the question of final liability would be settled through arbitration. The Bench also refused Echelon's request to put the judgment on hold.

title: Tiger Shroff Firing Incident: Three accused arrested by Kota police while travelling on Pune-Jaipur express
raw_summary:
Three men accused of being involved in the firing incident targeting Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai have been apprehended by the Kota City Police in Rajasthan. According to Kota Superintendent of Police Tejaswani Gautam, the three suspects were travelling on the Pune-Jaipur Express when the police team intercepted them. Two of the accused are from Haryana, while the third is from Bihar.

Speaking about the operation with ANI, Kota SP Tejaswani Gautam said the police received information about the suspects on Monday morning and acted swiftly to apprehend them. She said, "This morning, we received information, prompting us to activate our team. We learned that the three primary suspects involved in the firing were travelling by train and were due to arrive in Kota. Acting on this information, our team, within just 15 minutes, set a trap and thoroughly searched the entire train. Through this swift action by the Kota City Police, we have apprehended all three suspects responsible for the firing. We will soon hand the suspects over to the Mumbai Police. The names of these three individuals are: Rehan, alias Sukka, from Sonipat, Haryana; Hritik Kurmi, alias Roshan, from Begusarai, Bihar, who had been residing in Mumbai, Maharashtra, for the past few years; and one minor. We have apprehended and detained all three, and we will now hand them over to the Mumbai Police."

Gautam further explained that the police covered exit points, platforms and other locations to apprehend the suspects. The team received information at around 9:45 am, and the Mumbai Police have since arrived to take custody of the accused.

Providing details of the preliminary questioning, Gautam said, "Based on preliminary questioning, one of the accused is a Rapido rider. Further detailed interrogation will provide more clarity. The other two, one of whom is a minor and the other, Rehan, work as labourers in Sonipat. Preliminary questioning revealed that they intended to travel to Delhi by this train and then escape to Nepal from there. Rehan had previously been in contact with Anil Pandit..."

The firing incident took place at around 7 pm on Sunday when Tiger Shroff was leaving a football club in Mumbai's Juhu area. According to Mumbai Police, the accused allegedly opened fire at the actor's car. While Tiger escaped direct gunshot injuries, his driver sustained injuries in the incident.

Sources in the Mumbai Police Crime Branch indicated that the attack may have been planned after the accused monitored the actor's movements. The shooters allegedly knew that Tiger regularly visited the Juhu football ground on Sundays and had conducted reconnaissance before carrying out the attack. Following the firing, they reportedly travelled along SV Road through Vile Parle and Andheri, abandoned their motorcycle near Andheri West railway station and boarded a train towards Borivali. Preliminary intelligence suggested that the suspects subsequently crossed the Maharashtra border to evade law enforcement.

Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde visited Tiger's residence on Sunday night following the incident. He said the actor had sustained injuries to his left hand from gunpowder and glass fragments. Shinde also stated that Tiger and his mother, Ayesha Shroff, were shaken by the incident and assured them of the state government's support.

Speaking about the incident, Shinde said, "Strict action will be taken, and threats against public figures will not be tolerated."

Meanwhile, security outside Salman Khan's residence at Galaxy Apartments in Mumbai's Bandra area has been tightened following the firing incident. Police personnel wearing bulletproof jackets, along with police vehicles, were seen outside the actor's residence.

The case includes charges under Sections 109(1) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with Sections 3 and 25 of the Arms Act. The three suspects are expected to be handed over to the Mumbai Police for further investigation.

title: Imran Khan’s plea against ‘Leave India’ notice to be heard on October 26; Bombay High Court seeks Maharashtra government’s inclusion
raw_summary:
The Bombay High Court will hear actor Imran Khan’s petition challenging a directive issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) asking him to leave India on October 26. The actor has challenged the October 14 notice, arguing that it was issued without giving him a prior hearing and violated his rights as an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholder.

The matter was mentioned before a division bench comprising Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna on Monday. Senior advocate Venkatesh Dhond, appearing for Khan, told the court that the actor had received the notice after attempting to attend a protest, where he was stopped midway and had to return.

Dhond informed the bench that the Central government had been served a copy of the petition and requested an early hearing on October 21. However, the court scheduled the matter for October 26 to allow the FRRO time to obtain instructions on the petition.

During the hearing, the bench also asked Khan’s lawyers to implead the Maharashtra government as a party to the case so that the court could ascertain whether the actor had any criminal antecedents.

“Are there any criminal antecedents? Join State as party, so that in case. This is a local matter. So make State of Maharashtra a party,” the court said. Why Imran Khan challenged the FRRO notice In his petition, Khan has questioned the circumstances and manner in which the October 14 directive was issued. He has alleged that the authorities acted in haste without giving him an opportunity to present his case and bypassed the statutory protections available to him as an OCI cardholder. The actor has also claimed that the action followed social media campaigns targeting him by political figures.

According to the petition, the authorities issued the directive under public pressure rather than through an independent assessment of the circumstances. Khan has sought the quashing of the October 14 notice and an interim stay on its operation. He has also asked the court to restrain authorities from taking coercive steps, including deportation, issuing lookout notices, blacklisting him or interfering with his OCI status.

Additionally, the actor has sought the production of internal records relating to the decision to direct him to leave India. What led to the ‘Leave India’ notice? The directive was issued after Khan was briefly detained by the police following his participation in demonstrations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

The notice came shortly after Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Kirit Somaiya filed a first information report (FIR) at Mumbai’s Gamdevi police station, alleging public-order violations under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

Khan’s petition, filed on October 17, questions the speed with which the FRRO issued the directive following these developments. He has argued that the authorities failed to follow the procedure required before taking action that could affect his ability to remain in India. Imran Khan challenges notice, not OCI cancellation proceedings The actor’s petition also raises questions about the legal safeguards available to OCI cardholders. It argues that the FRRO bypassed Section 7D of the Citizenship Act, which provides for the cancellation of OCI registration on specified grounds and requires the prescribed procedure to be followed.

On October 17, the FRRO separately issued a show-cause notice asking Khan why his OCI registration should not be cancelled under Section 7D of the Citizenship Act. However, the actor has not challenged that notice in the present petition.

The distinction is significant because the October 14 directive asking him to leave India and the subsequent show-cause notice concerning his OCI registration are separate actions.

Together, the two films amassed nearly Rs. 2,200 crores globally, reaffirming his position as one of Indian cinema's biggest superstars. Three years later, Shah Rukh Khan is gearing up for his next theatrical release, King, directed by Siddharth Anand and scheduled to hit cinemas on December 24, 2026.

The excitement surrounding King is understandable. The film reunites Shah Rukh Khan with his Pathaan director, promises high-octane action and features an ensemble cast including Deepika Padukone, Suhana Khan and Abhishek Bachchan. However, beneath all the anticipation lies an interesting question: Has Shah Rukh Khan raised the bar so extraordinarily high that even a hugely successful film might now be considered a disappointment?

Before Pathaan and Jawan, a worldwide collection of Rs. 300-400 crores was considered an impressive achievement for many Bollywood films. But Shah Rukh Khan changed the conversation by delivering two consecutive Rs. 1,000 crore blockbusters, and in doing so, possibly created an unusually high benchmark for himself.

Today, the discussion around King isn't merely about whether it will succeed. Fans and trade observers are already speculating about whether it can cross Rs. 1,000 crores, surpass Pathaan or even challenge Jawan. Imagine a scenario where King collects Rs. 600-700 crores worldwide. Such numbers would be extraordinary for most Hindi films, yet there is a possibility that sections of the industry and social media would term the performance underwhelming simply because Shah Rukh Khan has delivered bigger hits in the past.

Ironically, King may find its biggest competition not in another film or superstar, but in Shah Rukh Khan's own box-office records.

Adding to the expectations is the film's reported scale. In July, Bollywood Hungama reported that King was being mounted on a production budget of approximately Rs. 450 crores, excluding publicity expenses and Shah Rukh Khan's remuneration. Siddharth Anand subsequently disputed the circulating budget reports, and hence, the actual cost remains unconfirmed. Nevertheless, the film is being positioned as an ambitious action spectacle, and its commercial performance will naturally attract considerable attention.

Its December 24 release also comes with challenges. The Christmas and New Year holidays provide an excellent opportunity for a huge opening, but December 2026 is packed with major releases, including Hollywood spectacles like Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part Three. Competition for screens and premium formats could affect King, particularly if the film hopes to enjoy the kind of extended theatrical run that helped Pathaan and Jawan achieve their historic numbers.

Shah Rukh Khan's prolonged absence from cinemas could work in his favour, as audiences haven't seen him in a leading theatrical role since Dunki (2023). However, there is an important difference between his return with Pathaan and his upcoming release.

Pathaan marked his comeback after a difficult phase at the box office, and audiences were eager to see whether he could reclaim his position. With King, there is no such question about his stardom. Instead, audiences are expecting another spectacular entertainer, complete with memorable dialogues, breathtaking action and larger-than-life moments.

The reunion with Siddharth Anand adds to these expectations. Having delivered a historic blockbuster together, the two will inevitably face comparisons with Pathaan. The challenge for King will be to offer something fresh rather than merely recreate the formula that worked so brilliantly in 2023.

The film also marks Shah Rukh Khan's much-anticipated big-screen collaboration with his daughter Suhana Khan, which will generate additional curiosity. However, for the film to succeed beyond the initial excitement, its story, performances and emotional appeal will have to connect with audiences.

If King earns Rs. 700 crores worldwide instead of Rs. 1,000 crores, it wouldn't automatically make the film a failure. Its actual profitability would depend on production costs, distribution arrangements, marketing expenditure and revenues from digital, satellite and music rights. A film can deliver impressive gross collections without necessarily generating equally impressive returns, while a relatively smaller grosser can be highly profitable if its costs are controlled.

The irony is that Pathaan and Jawan, the very films that re-established Shah Rukh Khan's box-office dominance, could now become the benchmarks against which every subsequent release is measured. If King delivers another Rs. 1,000 crore blockbuster, it will further cement his extraordinary legacy. But if it earns substantially less while still emerging as a major commercial success, should it really be viewed as a disappointment?

After all, no actor, irrespective of his superstardom, can be expected to deliver an all-time blockbuster with every release.

Perhaps the biggest danger surrounding King isn't that Shah Rukh Khan might fail to deliver another blockbuster. It's that Bollywood has reached a stage where even a blockbuster from Shah Rukh Khan may no longer be considered good enough.

title: EXCLUSIVE: CBFC censors shot of blood on the Indian map in Udta Teer

Udta Teer stars Ayushmann Khurrana, Sara Ali Khan, the late Mukul Dev and several others. Written and directed by Akash A Kaushik, the film is produced by Karan Johar, Adar Poonawalla and Apoorva Mehta's Dharma Productions, along with Guneet Monga Kapoor and Achin Jain's Sikhya Entertainment.

The film tells the story of a Pakistani spy who infiltrates India but ends up losing his memory. In an unexpected turn of events, he begins believing that he is a hardcore Indian patriot, leading to chaos and madness.

title: Sony LIV joins Prime Video India as an add-on subscription; plans start at Rs 399 per month
raw_summary:
Prime Video India has added Sony LIV to its list of add-on subscriptions, allowing customers to access the streaming platform’s movies, original series, television shows and live sports through a single service. Announced on October 21, the partnership gives viewers another option to access Sony LIV’s content without switching between separate apps.

Sony LIV will be available to Prime Video customers through two subscription plans priced at Rs 399 per month and Rs 1,499 per year. The service can be accessed through mobile devices, web browsers, Fire TV, smart TVs and other compatible living room devices.

The partnership brings Sony LIV’s library of more than 450 movies and 300 shows to Prime Video’s entertainment offering, alongside its live sports coverage and multilingual programming. What can viewers watch through Sony LIV on Prime Video? Sony LIV’s catalogue includes original series such as the Scam franchise and Gullak, along with films such as Sitaare Zameen Par. The service also offers popular television programmes from Sony Entertainment Television and Sony SAB, including Kaun Banega Crorepati, Indian Idol, Taarak Mehta Ka Ooltah Chashmah and Pushpa Impossible.

Reality and entertainment programming available through the platform includes KBC Season 18, Indian Idol Season 17 and Family Full House With Rohit Sharma.

Sports coverage is another key part of the partnership. Sony LIV offers live coverage of bilateral India cricket, the UEFA Champions League, the French Open, the Commonwealth Games and UFC, among other sporting events.

The announcement also highlighted India's upcoming tour of New Zealand, featuring Test matches, One Day Internationals and T20 Internationals, beginning October 22.

With content available in Hindi, English, Marathi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam and Gujarati, the partnership further expands the range of regional and international entertainment accessible through Prime Video. Prime Video and Sony LIV on the partnership Commenting on the development, Gaurav Bhasin, Head of AVOD Business and Marketplace at Prime Video India, said the addition would give customers access to a wider selection of entertainment and sports content.

“Our ambition has always been to make Prime Video the ultimate entertainment destination for our customers. With Sony LIV now available as an add-on subscription, we take a significant step forward in that journey,” Bhasin said.

He added that the partnership combines television programming and live sports with Prime Video’s existing catalogue.

“Along with our extensive library, customers now have the daily viewing cadence of television and a near-continuous calendar of live sports, from bilateral India cricket to the UEFA Champions League, all on one service. This deepens the breadth and choice of multilingual entertainment we offer, and we are excited about what it means for the millions of entertainment and sports fans across India,” he added.

Rajesh Kaul, Chief Revenue Officer and Business Head, Sports and International at Sony Pictures Networks India, said the partnership would help Sony LIV reach audiences through another platform.

“At Sony LIV, we’re always looking for new ways to make our content available to audiences wherever they choose to watch it. Our partnership with Prime Video is an important step in expanding that reach in India. It gives viewers another convenient way to discover and access Sony LIV's diverse content offering,” Kaul said.

He also highlighted the platform’s television programming, regional content, live sports and original series as important parts of its offering.

“Live sports and our slate of acclaimed Originals remain key to our proposition. Through this association, we look forward to taking the breadth of Sony LIV's entertainment and sports offering to more viewers across India and the world,” he added. How Prime Video add-on subscriptions work The addition of Sony LIV expands Prime Video’s selection of third-party subscriptions. The service allows customers to browse content from participating streaming platforms in one place rather than managing each service separately.

According to Prime Video, add-on subscriptions also offer consolidated billing, a shared watchlist, a download library for offline viewing and personalised recommendations. Customers can manage their subscriptions through Prime Video, although individual content catalogues and subscription terms may vary by provider.

title: Tiger Shroff’s team issues statement after firing in Juhu, says actor made “no statements” about incident

The team said in its statement, “We would like to categorically clarify that Tiger Shroff has made no statements, released no videos, and authorised no communication regarding the recent incident or any related developments.”

It further alleged that several social media pages and digital platforms were sharing fabricated stories and AI-generated videos while presenting them as statements or reactions from the actor.

The statement read, “It has come to our attention that several social media pages and digital platforms are circulating fabricated stories, AI-generated videos and scripted narratives, falsely attributed to Tiger. These are completely false, unauthorised and intended to mislead the public.”

Team Tiger also made it clear that neither the actor nor his team had any association with such material.

“We do not endorse, support, or have any association with such content,” the statement said.
